notes.text: Part a asserts that F prime is a figure, first showing its support equals the support of F and then splitting the minimal-containing-element argument into x in support G and x outside that support.
Part b changes raffine to above-line subdivise. After a cancelled attempt, it restates a least-containing-element condition and a closed-intersection/union-of-strata condition.
No mathematical correctness was used to fill the page. In particular, no qui est was supplied after the doubtful le/lui word even though the resulting phrase can be grammatically awkward.
If lui is confirmed, the literal continuation is c’est lui plus petit él. de F ...; retain it. The expected le is kept only as a glyph alternative, not imposed by syntax.
The accented à in à fortiori and the two de-like groups in the cancelled lower row are retained without normalizing.
H’s cf. définition de F minus G and qui est before plus petit have no corresponding ink at those locations. The actual parenthesis is et à fortiori de F minus G after él. de F.

The slanted a un plus petit addition has its own crop and is inside the subsequently cancelled block. Its leader reaches the abbreviated élément region; precise chronology/replacement scope should remain available for main/blind adjudication.

The isolated support equality initially invited a superset-equals doubt because of its hooked upper stroke. The b-heading equality has the same hooked two-stroke form, so = is retained. This was handwriting comparison, not a proof check.

All 19 C deleted scopes and all 3 C inserted scopes were explicitly audited, including the nested cancelled initial sign and the insertion cancelled again. No independent margin note, diagram, drawing or underline was found on this page.

No OCR, automated text recognition, external research, other-page inspection or TeX compilation was used. All witness agreements were read in the two halves; crop inspections address every C/H word difference and every unresolved source-state/formula locus.
